blogs.title: Beyond the GI Upset: Recognizing Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy as a Rare GLP-1 Agonist Complication
blogs.description: This post explores the emerging safety signal linking GLP-1 receptor agonists (like semaglutide) to severe neuromuscular toxicity. We will contrast the typical transient rhabdomyolysis seen with direct drug toxicity against the delayed, progressive, and autoimmune nature of Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy (IMNM). Key teaching points include recognizing the 'smoldering' timeline where weakness worsens months after exposure, distinguishing this from simple deconditioning or statin-myopathy, and understanding why standard drug withdrawal alone is insufficient for IMNM compared to toxic rhabdomyolysis.

blogs.title: The Seronegative Trap: Diagnosing IMNM When the Autoantibody Panel Comes Back Negative
blogs.description: A deep dive into the diagnostic challenges of seronegative IMNM. Using this case of a patient negative for anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibodies, we discuss why a negative myositis panel does not rule out autoimmune myopathy. The post will review critical histological hallmarks on muscle biopsy (necrotic fibers with macrophage infiltration but paucity of lymphocytes, MAC deposition) that confirm the diagnosis even in the absence of serology. We will also address how to differentiate these findings from polymyositis, dermatomyositis, and pure toxic myopathies in the emergency and inpatient settings.

blogs.title: Short-Course Salvation: Can Brief Immunosuppression Cure Drug-Induced IMNM?
blogs.description: This article analyzes the unique treatment trajectory of drug-triggered IMNM versus idiopathic forms. While idiopathic IMNM often requires years of aggressive immunosuppression, this case highlights a potential 'exit strategy' for medication-induced cases: removal of the trigger combined with a finite course of steroids and IVIG. We will examine the evidence for rapid tapering in drug-associated cases, the role of IVIG as a steroid-sparing agent in severe bulbar involvement, and monitoring strategies to ensure sustained remission without long-term immunosuppressive burden.

blogs.title: Heart vs. Muscle: Decoding Elevated Troponin and Transaminases in Severe Myopathy
blogs.description: Clinicians often panic when seeing elevated troponins and liver enzymes in a weak patient, fearing concurrent myocarditis or hepatic failure. This post uses the case's cardiac MRI and liver biopsy results to teach the art of differentiation. We will discuss how massive skeletal muscle breakdown can mimic liver injury (AST>ALT patterns) and cause false-positive troponin elevations due to cross-reactivity or demand ischemia rather than primary myocarditis. Learn how to utilize specific biomarkers (CK-MM vs. CK-MB), imaging nuances, and clinical context to avoid unnecessary cardiac workups or misdiagnosis of multi-organ failure.

blogs.title: The Obesity Paradox: Navigating Muscle Loss and Metabolic Therapy in the GLP-1 Era
blogs.description: As GLP-1 agonists become ubiquitous for obesity management, clinicians face a new paradox: achieving weight loss while preserving functional muscle mass. This post broadens the scope from this specific case to discuss the phenomenon of sarcopenic obesity exacerbated by rapid weight loss agents. We will explore screening tools for early muscle weakness in bariatric patients, counseling strategies regarding protein intake and resistance training alongside pharmacotherapy, and red flags that suggest a transition from physiological adaptation to pathological myopathy.
